paraphrase: Chapter 13 (35 verses in this edition; 34 in the 700-verse vulgate, which lacks 13.1) distinguishes the field (kṣetra) from its knower (kṣetrajña). Movements: 13.1 Arjuna asks about prakṛti and puruṣa, the field and its knower, knowledge and the knowable. 13.2–5 Kṛṣṇa calls the body the field and the one who knows it the knower of the field, declares himself the knower in all fields, calls the knowledge of both 'knowledge', and says this has been sung by the seers, in the metres and in the brahmasūtra words. 13.6–7 the field listed with its modifications (the great elements, ahaṅkāra, buddhi, the unmanifest, the senses and their ranges, desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, the aggregate, sentience, steadiness). 13.8–12 twenty dispositions, from absence of pride to keeping in view the aim of knowledge of reality, are declared 'knowledge'; what differs from them is ignorance. 13.13–19 the knowable: the beginningless supreme brahman, called neither being nor non-being, with hands, feet and eyes everywhere, without guṇas yet experiencing them, inside and outside beings, undivided yet as if divided, light of lights, set in the heart of all; knowing this the devotee becomes fit for Kṛṣṇa's state. 13.20–24 prakṛti and puruṣa are both beginningless; prakṛti is the cause in agency, puruṣa in experiencing; attachment to the guṇas causes births; the highest puruṣa in the body is named onlooker, consenter, supporter, experiencer, great lord and supreme self; one who knows this is not born again. 13.25–26 some see the self by meditation, others by sāṃkhya-yoga, others by karma-yoga; others worship on hearing from others and they too cross death. 13.27–35 every being is born from the union of field and knower; one who sees the supreme lord the same in all beings, prakṛti as doer and the self as non-doer, and the many resting in the one, truly sees and attains brahman; the supreme self, beginningless and without guṇas, neither acts nor is tainted, like space, and illumines the field as the sun the world; those who know the difference of field and knower with the eye of knowledge go to the supreme. The purpose the chapter states: knowledge of the field and its knower and of their difference (13.3, 13.35).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Chapter-level entry. Refs follow this edition: for 13.2–35 the vulgate number is one lower. Arjuna speaks 13.1; Kṛṣṇa speaks the rest.

original.text:
prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ caiva kṣetraṃ kṣetrajñameva ca|
etadveditumicchāmi jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ ca keśava
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Arjuna said: Prakṛti and puruṣa, the field (kṣetra) and the knower of the field (kṣetrajña), knowledge (jñāna) and what is to be known (jñeya) — this, Keśava, I wish to know.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Extra verse, absent from the 700-verse vulgate (no vulgate number); because of it this edition's chapter-13 numbering runs one higher than the vulgate. The verse frames the chapter: the six topics it names are answered in a different order — field and knower 13.2–7, knowledge 13.8–12, the knowable 13.13–19, prakṛti and puruṣa 13.20–24.

original.text: śrī bhagavānuvācaidaṃ śarīraṃ kaunteya kṣetramityabhidhīyate|etadyo vetti taṃ prāhuḥ kṣetrajña iti tadvidaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: The Blessed Lord said: This body (śarīra), son of Kuntī, is called 'the field' (kṣetra). The one who knows it, those who know these matters (tadvid) call 'the knower of the field' (kṣetrajña).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: = 13.1 in the 700-verse numbering. The segment's text begins with the speaker formula 'śrī bhagavān uvāca' fused to the first word (idaṃ). Both names are given as what others call them (abhidhīyate; prāhuḥ … tadvidaḥ).

original.text:
kṣetrajñaṃ cāpi māṃ viddhi sarvakṣetreṣu bhārata|
kṣetrakṣetrajñayorjñānaṃ yattajjñānaṃ mataṃ mama
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: And know me also as the knower of the field (kṣetrajña) in all fields, Bhārata. The knowledge of the field and of the knower of the field — that, in my view, is knowledge (jñāna).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: = 13.2 in the 700-verse numbering. 'Know me also (api) as the kṣetrajña in all fields': the commentators divide — Śaṅkara reads identity of the knower of the field with the Lord (difference only through limiting adjuncts); Rāmānuja reads the Lord as the self of all individual knowers, who are his body; dualist readings keep the Lord distinct from the individual knower. The paraphrase keeps the verse's own wording.

original.text: tatkṣetraṃ yacca yādṛk ca yadvikāri yataśca yat|sa ca yo yatprabhāvaśca tatsamāsena me śrṛṇu
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Hear from me in brief what that field is, of what kind, what its modifications (vikāra) are, and what comes from what (yataś ca yat); and who he (the knower of the field) is, and what his powers (prabhāva) are.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: = 13.3 in the 700-verse numbering. Announcement of the topic. 'yataś ca yat' is terse ('and from what, what'); the commentators take it as the causes and effects within the field. The segment spells 'śrṛṇu' for śṛṇu.

original.text: ṛṣibhirbahudhā gītaṃ chandobhirvividhaiḥ pṛthak|brahmasūtrapadaiścaiva hetumadbhirviniśicataiḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: It has been sung by the seers (ṛṣi) in many ways, separately in various metres (chandas), and also in the words of the brahmasūtras (brahmasūtrapada), which give reasons (hetumat) and are decisive (viniścita).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: = 13.4 in the 700-verse numbering. brahmasūtrapadaiḥ: the commentators divide — Śaṅkara takes it as the Upaniṣadic sentences that indicate brahman, Rāmānuja as the (Śārīraka) Brahma Sūtras; the paraphrase leaves the compound untranslated. chandobhiḥ: 'by metres', i.e. Vedic hymns. The segment spells 'viniśicataiḥ' for viniścitaiḥ.

original.text: mahābhūtānyahaṅkāro buddhiravyaktameva ca|indriyāṇi daśaikaṃ ca pañca cendriyagocarāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: The great elements (mahābhūta), the I-maker (ahaṅkāra), the intellect (buddhi) and the unmanifest (avyakta); the ten senses (indriya) and the one; and the five ranges of the senses (indriyagocara) —
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: = 13.5 in the 700-verse numbering. The sentence continues in 13.7, which calls the whole list 'the field'. 'The one' after the ten senses is taken by the commentators as manas; the verse does not name it. Counting the great elements as five, the items make the twenty-four principles familiar from Sāṃkhya, but the verse neither numbers them nor names a school.

original.text: icchā dveṣaḥ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ saṅghātaścetanādhṛtiḥ|etatkṣetraṃ samāsena savikāramudāhṛtam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: — desire (icchā), aversion (dveṣa), pleasure (sukha), pain (duḥkha), the aggregate (saṅghāta), sentience (cetanā) and steadiness (dhṛti): this, in brief, is declared to be the field together with its modifications (savikāra).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: = 13.6 in the 700-verse numbering. cetanā (sentience, awareness) is listed here as part of the field, not as its knower; the commentators explain it as a state of the body-mind aggregate in which awareness shows. saṅghāta: the aggregate (of body and organs). The verse does not settle whether icchā etc. are the 'modifications' or further members of the field.

original.text: amānitvamadambhitvamahiṃsā kṣāntirārjavam|ācāryopāsanaṃ śaucaṃ sthairyamātmavinigrahaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Absence of pride (amānitva), absence of pretension (adambhitva), non-harming (ahiṃsā), forbearance (kṣānti), uprightness (ārjava), attendance on the teacher (ācāryopāsana), purity (śauca), steadfastness (sthairya), restraint of oneself (ātmavinigraha) —
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: = 13.7 in the 700-verse numbering. Opens the list (13.8–12, vulgate 13.7–11) that 13.12 names 'knowledge' (jñāna). ātmavinigraha is reflexive: restraint of oneself (the commentators: of body, senses and mind).

original.text: indriyārtheṣu vairāgyamanahaṅkāra eva ca|janmamṛtyujarāvyādhiduḥkhadoṣānudarśanam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: — dispassion (vairāgya) toward the objects of the senses (indriyārtha), absence of the I-maker (anahaṅkāra), and seeing again and again the evil (doṣa) of birth, death, old age, sickness and pain (duḥkha) —
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: = 13.8 in the 700-verse numbering. The compound janma-mṛtyu-jarā-vyādhi-duḥkha-doṣa-anudarśana can also be divided 'seeing the pain and the evil in birth, death, old age and sickness'.

original.text: asakitaranabhiṣvaṅgaḥ putradāragṛhādiṣu|nityaṃ ca samacittatvamiṣṭāniṣṭopapattiṣu
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: — non-attachment (asakti) and absence of clinging (anabhiṣvaṅga) toward son, wife, home and the like; and constant evenness of citta (samacittatva) when what is wanted or unwanted befalls —
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: = 13.9 in the 700-verse numbering. The syntax does not settle whether 'toward son, wife, home and the like' governs asakti as well as anabhiṣvaṅga; the commentators give asakti a general sense and anabhiṣvaṅga the specific one.

original.text: mayi cānanyayogena bhakitaravyabhicāriṇī|viviktadeśasevitvamaratirjanasaṃsadi
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: — unswerving devotion (bhakti avyabhicāriṇī) to me through a yoga that has no other (ananya-yoga); resorting to secluded places (viviktadeśa-sevitva); lack of delight in gatherings of people (arati janasaṃsadi) —
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: = 13.10 in the 700-verse numbering. Devotion to the speaker is counted here among the marks of 'knowledge'. ananyayogena, 'by a yoga with no other': the commentators gloss it as exclusive devotion with no other goal or refuge, or as undivided, non-separate concentration. The segment spells 'bhakitar' for bhaktir.

original.text: adhyātmajñānanityatvaṃ tattvajñānārthadarśanam|etajjñānamiti proktamajñānaṃ yadatonyathā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: — constancy in knowledge of what pertains to the self (adhyātma-jñāna), and keeping in view the aim (artha) of the knowledge of reality (tattvajñāna): this is declared to be knowledge (jñāna); what is other than this is ignorance (ajñāna).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: = 13.11 in the 700-verse numbering. Closes the list begun at 13.8: the whole set of dispositions from amānitva onward is called 'knowledge'. tattvajñānārthadarśana: artha as the goal/purpose of that knowledge (the commentators: liberation) or as its object.

original.text: jñeyaṃ yattatpravakṣyāmi yajjñātvā'mṛtamaśnute|anādimatparaṃ brahma na sattannāsaducyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: I will declare that which is to be known (jñeya), knowing which one attains the immortal (amṛta): the beginningless supreme brahman (anādimat paraṃ brahma). It is said to be neither being (sat) nor non-being (asat).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: = 13.12 in the 700-verse numbering. Word-division is disputed: 'anādimat paraṃ' (beginningless, supreme) or 'anādi matparaṃ' (beginningless, having me as the highest) — Śaṅkara mentions and rejects the second, Rāmānuja adopts it. The commentators also differ on what 'the knowable' is here (the supreme brahman for Śaṅkara; for Rāmānuja the self in its pure nature, whose highest is the Lord). 'Neither sat nor asat' is stated, not argued.

original.text: sarvataḥ pāṇipādaṃ tatsarvato'kṣiśiromukham|sarvataḥ śrutimalloke sarvamāvṛtya tiṣṭhati
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: It has hands and feet everywhere, eyes, heads and faces everywhere, ears everywhere in the world; it stands enveloping all.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: = 13.13 in the 700-verse numbering. Nearly identical with Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad 3.16. The subject is the knowable brahman of 13.13.

original.text: sarvendriyaguṇābhāsaṃ sarvendriyavivarjitam|asaktaṃ sarvabhṛccaiva nirguṇaṃ guṇabhoktṛ ca
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: It appears through the qualities (guṇa) of all the senses, yet is devoid of all the senses; it is unattached (asakta), yet supports all; it is without guṇas (nirguṇa), yet the experiencer of the guṇas (guṇabhoktṛ).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: = 13.14 in the 700-verse numbering. The first half matches Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad 3.17a. 'sarvendriyaguṇābhāsam' can be read 'shining through (illumining) the functions of all the senses' or 'having the semblance of the sense-qualities'. Each positive predicate is paired with a negation; the verse does not say which description is the higher.

original.text: bahirantaśca bhūtānāmacaraṃ carameva ca|sūkṣmatvāttadavijñeyaṃ dūrasthaṃ cāntike ca tat
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: It is outside and inside beings; it is the unmoving and also the moving; because of its subtlety (sūkṣmatva) it is not to be known (avijñeya); it is far off and it is near.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: = 13.15 in the 700-verse numbering. Compare Īśa Upaniṣad 5 (tad dūre tad v antike; tad antar asya sarvasya tad u sarvasyāsya bāhyataḥ). avijñeya is said of what 13.13 calls 'the knowable'; the commentators add 'by the undiscerning' or 'as an object of the senses'.

original.text: avibhaktaṃ ca bhūteṣu vibhaktamiva ca sthitam|bhūtabhartṛ ca tajjñeyaṃ grasiṣṇu prabhaviṣṇu ca
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Undivided (avibhakta), it yet stands in beings as if divided; that knowable (jñeya) is the sustainer of beings (bhūtabhartṛ), and their devourer and their generator.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: = 13.16 in the 700-verse numbering.

original.text: jyotiṣāmapi tajjyotistamasaḥ paramucyate|jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ jñānagamyaṃ hṛdi sarvasya viṣṭhitam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: It is the light even of lights, and is said to be beyond darkness (tamas); it is knowledge (jñāna), the knowable (jñeya), and what is to be reached by knowledge (jñānagamya), set in the heart of all.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: = 13.17 in the 700-verse numbering. tamasaḥ param, 'beyond darkness' (compare ŚvetU 3.8 ādityavarṇaṃ tamasaḥ parastāt): tamas here is darkness, not the guṇa of chapter 14. 'jyotiṣām api taj jyotiḥ' echoes BĀU 4.4.16 (jyotiṣāṃ jyotiḥ).

original.text: iti kṣetraṃ tathā jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ coktaṃ samāsataḥ|madbhakta etadvijñāya madbhāvāyopapadyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Thus the field, and likewise knowledge and the knowable, have been told in brief. My devotee (madbhakta), knowing this, becomes fit for my state of being (madbhāva).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: = 13.18 in the 700-verse numbering. Summary of 13.2–18 with its stated result. madbhāvāya upapadyate: 'becomes fit for / reaches my state' — the commentators gloss madbhāva as the state of the supreme self (liberation) or as a mode of being like the Lord's.

original.text: prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ caiva viddhyanādī ubhāvapi|vikārāṃśca guṇāṃścaiva viddhi prakṛtisaṃbhavān
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Know that prakṛti and puruṣa are both beginningless (anādi); and know that the modifications (vikāra) and the guṇas arise from prakṛti.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: = 13.19 in the 700-verse numbering. Takes up the pair named in 13.1. The verse does not say whether these are the Lord's two natures of 7.4–5 (as several commentators read them) or principles in their own right.

original.text: kāryakāraṇakartṛtve hetuḥ prakṛtirucyate|puruṣaḥ sukhaduḥkhānāṃ bhoktṛtve heturucyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Prakṛti is said to be the cause (hetu) in the agency (kartṛtva) regarding effects and instruments (kārya-kāraṇa); puruṣa is said to be the cause in the experiencing (bhoktṛtva) of pleasures and pains.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: = 13.20 in the 700-verse numbering. kārya-kāraṇa: the commentators take kārya as the body and kāraṇa (some editions read karaṇa) as the organs or instruments.

original.text: puruṣaḥ prakṛtistho hi bhuṅkte prakṛtijānguṇān|kāraṇaṃ guṇasaṅgo'sya sadasadyonijanmasu
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: For puruṣa, situated in prakṛti (prakṛtistha), experiences (bhuṅkte) the guṇas born of prakṛti; attachment to the guṇas (guṇasaṅga) is the cause of its births in good and bad wombs (sad-asad-yoni).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: = 13.21 in the 700-verse numbering.

original.text: upadraṣṭā'numantā ca bhartā bhoktā maheśvaraḥ|paramātmeti cāpyukto dehe'sminpuruṣaḥ paraḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: The highest puruṣa (puruṣaḥ paraḥ) in this body is also called the onlooker (upadraṣṭṛ), the consenter (anumantṛ), the supporter (bhartṛ), the experiencer (bhoktṛ), the great lord (maheśvara), and the supreme self (paramātman).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: = 13.22 in the 700-verse numbering. The commentators divide on whether 'the highest puruṣa in this body' is the experiencing puruṣa of 13.21–22 (vulgate 13.20–21) seen in its own higher nature, or the Lord present in the body as distinct from the experiencer; the verse gives both 'experiencer' and 'supreme self' among its names. anumantṛ: one who approves or permits.

original.text: ya evaṃ vetti puruṣaṃ prakṛtiṃ ca guṇaiḥsaha|sarvathā vartamāno'pi na sa bhūyo'bhijāyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: One who knows puruṣa in this way, and prakṛti together with the guṇas, is not born again, however he may be living (sarvathā vartamāno 'pi).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: = 13.23 in the 700-verse numbering. The phrase 'sarvathā vartamāno 'pi' also occurs at 6.31; the commentators limit its scope in different ways.

original.text: dhyānenātmani paśyanti kecidātmānamātmanā|anye sāṃkhyena yogena karmayogena cāpare
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Some, through meditation (dhyāna), see the self (ātmānam) in themselves (ātmani) by themselves (ātmanā); others by the yoga of sāṃkhya (sāṃkhya-yoga); and still others by the yoga of action (karma-yoga).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: = 13.24 in the 700-verse numbering. ātmani and ātmanā can be read reflexively ('in themselves', 'by themselves') or as 'in the self', 'by the self'; the commentators gloss them as the intellect and the purified mind. 'sāṃkhya' is the Gītā's own term (cf. 2.39, 3.3, 5.4–5), not necessarily the later classical school.

original.text: anye tvevamajānantaḥ śrutvā'nyebhya upāsate|te'pi cātitarantyeva mṛtyuṃ śrutiparāyaṇāḥ

paraphrase: Chapter 14 (27 verses) sets out the three guṇas. Movements: 14.1–2 Kṛṣṇa announces again the highest knowledge, by which the sages reached the highest perfection and came to share his nature, not born at creation nor troubled at dissolution. 14.3–4 the great brahman is his womb; he places the embryo in it and is the seed-giving father of all forms. 14.5–10 sattva, rajas and tamas, born of prakṛti, bind the embodied one — sattva by attachment to happiness and knowledge, rajas by attachment to action, tamas by heedlessness, idleness and sleep — and each prevails by overpowering the other two. 14.11–13 the signs of each when increased. 14.14–15 where one goes on dying in each. 14.16–18 their fruits and their upward, middle and downward courses. 14.19–20 one who sees no agent but the guṇas and knows what is beyond them attains Kṛṣṇa's state, and going beyond the three guṇas attains the immortal, freed from birth, death, old age and pain. 14.21 Arjuna asks the marks, the conduct and the means of one gone beyond the guṇas. 14.22–25 the marks and conduct: not hating or longing for the guṇas' effects, unshaken, knowing 'the guṇas operate', the same in pleasure and pain, praise and blame, honour and dishonour, friend and foe, relinquishing all undertakings. 14.26–27 the means: serving Kṛṣṇa with unswerving devotion one goes beyond the guṇas and becomes fit for becoming brahman — for he is the foundation of brahman, of the immortal, of everlasting dharma and of absolute happiness. The purpose the chapter states: knowledge of how the guṇas bind and of the way beyond them (14.1–2, 14.19–26).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Chapter-level entry. Arjuna speaks 14.21; Kṛṣṇa speaks the rest.

original.text: udāsīnavadāsīno guṇairyo na vicālyate|guṇā vartanta ityeva yo'vatiṣṭhati neṅgate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: — he who, sitting as one indifferent (udāsīnavat), is not shaken by the guṇas; who, (knowing) only that 'the guṇas are operating' (guṇā vartante), stays firm and does not waver —
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text: samaduḥkhasukhaḥ svasthaḥ samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ|tulyapriyāpriyo dhīrastulyanindātmasaṃstutiḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: — alike in pain and pleasure, abiding in himself (svastha), regarding a clod, a stone and gold as the same, the same toward the pleasant and the unpleasant, steadfast (dhīra), the same in blame and in praise of himself —
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: svastha and ātma-saṃstuti are reflexive: established in oneself; praise of oneself.

original.text: mānāpamānayostulyastulyo mitrāripakṣayoḥ|sarvārambhaparityāgī guṇātītaḥ sa ucyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: — the same in honour and dishonour, the same toward the side of friend and of foe, relinquishing all undertakings (sarvārambha-parityāgin): he is called one who has gone beyond the guṇas (guṇātīta).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: sarvārambhaparityāgī also at 12.16; the commentators restrict it to undertakings for desired ends.

original.text: māṃ ca yo'vyabhicāreṇa bhakitayogena sevate|sa guṇānsamatītyaitān brahmabhūyāya kalpate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: And he who serves (sevate) me with the unswerving yoga of devotion (avyabhicāra bhakti-yoga), having gone fully beyond these guṇas, becomes fit for becoming brahman (brahmabhūya).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Answers the third question of 14.21 (how one passes beyond the guṇas). 'brahmabhūyāya kalpate' recurs at 18.53. The segment spells 'bhakitayogena' for bhaktiyogena.

original.text: brahmaṇo hi pratiṣṭhā'hamamṛtasyāvyayasya ca|śāśvatasya ca dharmasya sukhasyaikāntikasya ca
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: For I am the foundation (pratiṣṭhā) of brahman, of the imperishable immortal (amṛta), of everlasting dharma, and of absolute (aikāntika) happiness (sukha).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: pratiṣṭhā: 'foundation, support, abode, basis'. 'amṛtasyāvyayasya ca' may stand in apposition to brahman or as a further item. The commentators divide on what 'brahman' denotes here (the supreme brahman, whose abode or basis the speaker as inner self is; the self in its pure state; or the impersonal brahman grounded in the personal Lord) and so on how the speaker is its pratiṣṭhā. The paraphrase keeps 'foundation'.

paraphrase: Chapter 15 (20 verses) moves from the world-tree to the highest person. Movements: 15.1–2 the imperishable aśvattha with roots above and branches below, its leaves the metres, its branches swollen by the guṇas with the sense-objects as shoots, its roots below bound up with action in the human world; to know it is to know the Veda. 15.3–6 its form, end, beginning and foundation are not perceived here; it is to be cut with the weapon of non-attachment and the place of no return sought, with the words 'I take refuge in that primal person'; those free of pride, delusion, attachment and desire, intent on the self and released from the pairs reach that imperishable place, unlit by sun, moon or fire, Kṛṣṇa's supreme abode. 15.7–11 an eternal portion of Kṛṣṇa, become the living being, draws the senses and mind, carries them from body to body as wind carries scents, and enjoys objects through them; the deluded do not see it, those with the eye of knowledge and striving yogins do. 15.12–15 Kṛṣṇa is the radiance in sun, moon and fire, sustains beings, nourishes plants as Soma, digests food as Vaiśvānara, is seated in the heart of all, the source of memory, knowledge and their loss, the one to be known by all the Vedas, maker of the vedānta and knower of the Veda. 15.16–20 there are two persons in the world, the perishable (all beings) and the imperishable (the one standing firm), and the highest person, another, called the supreme self, the imperishable lord; Kṛṣṇa, beyond the perishable and higher than the imperishable, is the puruṣottama; one who knows him so knows all and worships him with his whole being; this is the most secret teaching, understanding which one is wise and has done what is to be done. The purpose the chapter states: to make known the puruṣottama (15.18–20).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Chapter-level entry. Kṛṣṇa speaks throughout.

original.text: śrī bhagavānuvācaūrdhvamūlamadhaḥśākhamaśvatthaṃ prāhuravyayam|chandāṃsi yasya parṇāni yastaṃ veda sa vedavit
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: The Blessed Lord said: They speak of an imperishable (avyaya) aśvattha tree with its roots above and its branches below, whose leaves are the metres (chandas); one who knows it knows the Veda (vedavid).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Kaṭha Upaniṣad 2.3.1 (ūrdhvamūlo 'vākśākha eṣo 'śvatthaḥ sanātanaḥ) has the same inverted tree. 'prāhuḥ', 'they speak of': the image is presented as received. The verse does not say what the tree stands for; the commentators take it as saṃsāra and 'imperishable' as its beginningless continuity. The segment fuses the speaker formula to the verse.

original.text: adhaścordhvaṃ prasṛtāstasya śākhā     guṇapravṛddhā viṣayapravālāḥ|adhaśca mūlānyanusantatāni     karmānubandhīni manuṣyaloke
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Its branches spread below and above, swollen by the guṇas (guṇa-pravṛddha), with the objects of sense (viṣaya) as their shoots; and below, in the world of humans, its roots stretch on, bound up with action (karmānubandhin).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text: na rūpamasyeha tathopalabhyate    nānto na cādirna ca saṃpratiṣṭhā|aśvatthamenaṃ suvirūḍhamūla    masaṅgaśastreṇa dṛḍhena chittvā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Its form is not perceived here as such, nor its end, nor its beginning, nor its foundation (saṃpratiṣṭhā). Having cut this firmly rooted aśvattha with the strong weapon of non-attachment (asaṅga-śastra) —
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The sentence continues into 15.4.

original.text: tataḥ padaṃ tatparimārgitavya    yasmingatā na nivartanti bhūyaḥ|tameva cādyaṃ puruṣaṃ prapadye    yataḥ pravṛttiḥ prasṛtā purāṇī
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: — then that place (pada) is to be sought, having gone to which they do not return again: 'I take refuge (prapadye) in that very primal person (ādya puruṣa), from whom the ancient stream of activity (pravṛtti) flowed forth.'
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: prapadye is first person: a formula for the seeker ('saying: I take refuge …') or the speaker's own words; the commentators take it as the attitude in which the place is to be sought. The segment reads 'parimārgitavya' without the final anusvāra (parimārgitavyaṃ).

original.text: nirmānamohā jitasaṅgadoṣā    adhyātmanityā vinivṛttakāmāḥ|dvandvairvimuktāḥ sukhaduḥkhasaṃjñai    rgacchantyamūḍhāḥ padamavyayaṃ tat
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Free from pride (māna) and delusion (moha), having conquered the fault of attachment (saṅga-doṣa), constantly intent on what pertains to the self (adhyātma-nitya), with desires (kāma) turned away, released from the pairs of opposites (dvandva) known as pleasure and pain, the undeluded go to that imperishable place (padam avyayam).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text: na tadbhāsayate sūryo na śaśāṅko na pāvakaḥ|yadgatvā na nivartante taddhāma paramaṃ mama
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: The sun does not illumine it, nor the moon, nor fire: that, having gone to which they do not return, is my supreme abode (dhāma paramaṃ mama).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Compare Kaṭha 2.2.15, Śvetāśvatara 6.14 and Muṇḍaka 2.2 (na tatra sūryo bhāti …). 'tad dhāma paramaṃ mama' also closes 8.21.

original.text: mamaivāṃśo jīvaloke jīvabhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ|manaḥṣaṣṭhānīndriyāṇi prakṛtisthāni karṣati
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: A portion (aṃśa) of me alone, eternal (sanātana), having become the living being (jīvabhūta) in the world of the living (jīvaloka), draws to itself the senses, with the mind (manas) as the sixth, which abide in prakṛti.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The commentators divide on 'portion': an apparent part, like the sun reflected in water or space enclosed in a pot (Śaṅkara); a real part in the sense of a mode or body of the Lord (Rāmānuja); a separated part, eternally distinct (Madhva). The verse says 'a portion of me', not 'of brahman'. karṣati: draws, drags, attracts.

original.text: śarīraṃ yadavāpnoti yaccāpyutkrāmatīśvaraḥ|gṛhītvaitāni saṃyāti vāyurgandhānivāśayāt
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: When the lord (īśvara) — the living being of 15.7 — takes up a body and when he departs from it, he takes these (the senses and mind) and goes, as the wind carries scents from their seat (āśaya).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: īśvara here is, in context, the embodied being as master of the body and senses (so the commentators), not the supreme lord of 15.17.

original.text: śrotraṃ cakṣuḥ sparśanaṃ ca rasanaṃ ghrāṇameva ca|adhiṣṭhāya manaścāyaṃ viṣayānupasevate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Presiding over (adhiṣṭhāya) the ear, the eye, touch, taste and smell, and the mind (manas), he enjoys the objects of the senses (viṣaya).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text: utkrāmantaṃ sthitaṃ vāpi bhuñjānaṃ vā guṇānvitam|vimūḍhā nānupaśyanti paśyanti jñānacakṣuṣaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Whether he is departing, staying, or enjoying, joined with the guṇas — the deluded do not see him; those with the eye of knowledge (jñāna-cakṣus) see.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text: yatanto yoginaścainaṃ paśyantyātmanyavasthitam|yatanto'pyakṛtātmāno nainaṃ paśyantyacetasaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Striving yogins see him established in themselves (ātmani); but those who have not made themselves ready (akṛtātman), lacking understanding (acetas), do not see him even though they strive.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: ātmani, 'in themselves' or 'in the self'; akṛtātmānaḥ, 'whose selves (minds) are unformed' — both reflexive. acetas: 'without cetas' (undiscerning, thoughtless).

original.text: yadādityagataṃ tejo jagadbhāsayate'khilam|yaccandramasi yaccāgnau tattejo viddhi māmakam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: The radiance (tejas) that is in the sun and illumines the whole world, and that which is in the moon and in fire — know that radiance to be mine.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text: gāmāviśya ca bhūtāni dhārayāmyahamojasā|puṣṇāmi cauṣadhīḥ sarvāḥ somo bhūtvā rasātmakaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Entering the earth (go), I sustain beings by my vigour (ojas); and becoming Soma, whose nature is sap (rasātmaka), I nourish all plants.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The commentators take Soma here as the moon, whose sap nourishes plants; the verse says only 'having become Soma'.

original.text: ahaṃ vaiśvānaro bhūtvā prāṇināṃ dehamāśritaḥ|prāṇāpānasamāyuktaḥ pacāmyannaṃ caturvidham
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Becoming Vaiśvānara, dwelling in the bodies of breathing beings (prāṇin), joined with prāṇa and apāna, I digest (pacāmi, 'cook') the fourfold food.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Compare BĀU 5.9.1 (the vaiśvānara fire within a person, by which food is digested). The verse does not name the four kinds of food; the commentators list what is chewed, sucked, licked and swallowed.

original.text: sarvasya cāhaṃ hṛdi sanniviṣṭo    mattaḥ smṛtirjñānamapohanaṃ ca|vedaiśca sarvairahameva vedyo    vedāntakṛdvedavideva cāham
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: And I am seated in the heart of all; from me come memory (smṛti), knowledge (jñāna) and their loss (apohana). I alone am what is to be known by all the Vedas; I am the maker of the vedānta (vedāntakṛt) and the knower of the Veda (vedavid).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: apohana: 'removal, loss' (of memory and knowledge) for most commentators; some take it as reasoning (removal of doubt). vedāntakṛt: 'originator of the vedānta (the Upaniṣadic teaching or its tradition)' or 'the one who brings the Veda to its end, its fruit' — the commentators divide. 'hṛdi sanniviṣṭaḥ' echoes ŚvetU 3.13 / Kaṭha 2.3.17 (hṛdaye sanniviṣṭaḥ).

original.text: dvāvimau puruṣau loke kṣaraścākṣara eva ca|kṣaraḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni kūṭastho'kṣara ucyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: There are these two persons (puruṣa) in the world, the perishable (kṣara) and the imperishable (akṣara). The perishable is all beings; the one standing firm (kūṭastha) is called the imperishable.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The commentators divide on what the akṣara is here — e.g. Śaṅkara: the Lord's māyā-power, the seed of the perishable; Rāmānuja: the self freed from association with matter; others: the individual selves as such. The paraphrase keeps the text's terms. Compare ŚvetU 1.10 (kṣaraṃ pradhānam amṛtākṣaraṃ haraḥ).

original.text: uttamaḥ puruṣastvanyaḥ paramātmetyudāhṛtaḥ|yo lokatrayamāviśya bibhartyavyaya īśvaraḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: But the highest person (uttamaḥ puruṣaḥ) is another, called the supreme self (paramātman): the imperishable lord (avyaya īśvara) who, having entered the three worlds, sustains them.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'another' (anya): other than both the kṣara and the akṣara of 15.16. Compare ŚvetU 1.8 (saṃyuktam etat kṣaram akṣaraṃ ca … bharate viśvam īśaḥ).

original.text: yasmātkṣaramatīto'hamakṣarādapi cottamaḥ|ato'smi loke vede ca prathitaḥ puruṣottamaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Since I am beyond the perishable (kṣara) and higher even than the imperishable (akṣara), I am therefore renowned in the world and in the Veda as the highest person (puruṣottama).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: An argued statement (yasmāt … ataḥ). Compare Muṇḍaka 2.1.2 (akṣarāt parataḥ paraḥ). How 'higher than the akṣara' is understood depends on what the akṣara of 15.16 is taken to be.

original.text: yo māmevamasammūḍho jānāti puruṣottamam|sa sarvavidbhajati māṃ sarvabhāvena bhārata
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: One who, undeluded (asaṃmūḍha), knows me thus as the highest person (puruṣottama) knows all (sarvavid) and worships (bhajati) me with his whole being (sarvabhāvena), Bhārata.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Knowing the puruṣottama and worshipping him with one's whole being are joined in one sentence.

original.text: iti guhyatamaṃ śāstramidamuktaṃ mayā'nagha|etadbuddhvā buddhimānsyātkṛtakṛtyaśca bhārata
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Thus this most secret teaching (guhyatama śāstra) has been spoken by me, sinless one. Understanding it, one would be wise (buddhimat) and one who has done what is to be done (kṛtakṛtya), Bhārata.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Closing verse of chapter 15: praise (most secret) and stated result (kṛtakṛtya).
